title: A click anywhere in an unfolded tool call folds it
body:
An expandable tool call folds and unfolds on a click on its head row. `draw_transcript` in `ui.rs` records each head's rows on screen as a `FoldArea`, and `App`'s click handling folds the call whose `FoldArea` holds the click. When an unfolded call is taller than the transcript and its head has scrolled off the top, you have to scroll back up to fold it.

## Proposal

- A fold's `FoldArea` covers the call's whole drawn area, its head and its body.
- A click in the body still goes first to whatever is under it: a link, a copy button, the scroll bar, or a nested call's own head. The innermost fold under the click takes it.
- Hovering anywhere over a call that can fold shades the whole call with the palette's `tint`. The fold marker turns `accent` as now.

## Rejected

- A sticky head, pinned at the top of the transcript while its body is in view. It costs a row and a second drawing path. A click in the body covers the same need.

## Open

- coax-2eb9e5 may give a left drag in the transcript to text selection. A click with no drag would still fold, which can surprise someone who clicked to clear a selection.
close_reason: Done in a7ec3a2. `FoldArea::whole` takes body clicks after links, copy buttons, the head and pan bars, and the hovered call is painted with `tint`. Nested folds do not exist, since a subagent's children do not fold on their own, so the innermost-body rule was dropped.
